title: Case #001
question: Whose career is the evidence tracing?

suspects.label: Jon Stewart
suspects.whyPlausible: The answer: MTV alum, Kilborn's successor, Sonny's roommate, Crossfire's antagonist, sixteen years at one desk.

suspects.label: Craig Kilborn
suspects.whyPlausible: The designed trap: he is IN Old School, he sat at the same fake-news desk, and he moved shows in 1999. Survives almost to the end.

suspects.label: Stephen Colbert
suspects.whyPlausible: The same desk's most famous alumnus — fits the Daily Show exhibit completely.

suspects.label: Conan O'Brien
suspects.whyPlausible: The right era of late night, the right comedy pedigree.

suspects.label: David Letterman
suspects.whyPlausible: The defining late-night figure of the era — the default guess for any desk mystery.

suspects.label: Jay Leno
suspects.whyPlausible: The other half of every late-night argument of the 1990s.

suspects.label: Trevor Noah
suspects.whyPlausible: A Daily Show host — fits the desk exhibit for younger players.

suspects.label: Jimmy Fallon
suspects.whyPlausible: Modern late night's biggest mainstream name.

suspects.label: Adam Sandler
suspects.whyPlausible: Surges when Big Daddy's world appears — he IS Sonny. The exhibit is pointing at the man beside him.

suspects.label: Ben Stiller
suspects.whyPlausible: A genuine MTV alum — The Ben Stiller Show started there — so he survives the exhibit that kills Letterman and Leno.

authorNotes.meaning: A 2003 fraternity comedy — deliberately sideways. Craig Kilborn plays the smug boyfriend, and Kilborn is the arrow: the original host of the desk the answer made famous. As elimination work, nothing about a 2003 American frat comedy touches Trevor Noah's story.

Where the answer's television career began: You Wrote It, You Watch It (1992), then The Jon Stewart Show (1993), MTV's first talk show. It quietly rules out the network-establishment names — Letterman and Leno were never MTV people — while sparing Ben Stiller, whose sketch show genuinely started there. That's the designed trap inside the trap.

Big Daddy, 1999: Sonny Koufax adopts a five-year-old. Adam Sandler players surge here — but the exhibit is pointing at the man beside him. The answer played Kevin Gerrity, Sonny's roommate, the same year he took over a certain desk.

The institution. This one exhibit clears most of the board — Conan, Fallon, Sandler and Stiller have no claim to that desk. But it leaves the dangerous suspects standing: Kilborn hosted it first, Colbert rose from its correspondent bench, Noah inherited it later.

evidence.content: I'm not going to be your monkey.
evidence.caption: CNN, October 15, 2004.

authorNotes.meaning: The Crossfire appearance — the moment the answer stopped being just a comedian and became a media critic, on the air, to the hosts' faces. The date and the defiance fit no one else at that desk; Kilborn's era had nothing like it.
The smoking gun: the tenure. Kilborn left the desk at the end of 1998; Noah arrived in 2015; Colbert left for his own Report in 2005. Exactly one person sat there from 1999 to 2015.

hints.text: One suspect is inside one of the exhibits as an actor. He isn't the answer — he's the arrow.
The roommate exhibit is asking who was beside the star, not who the star was.
Take the dates literally: who sat at that desk for those sixteen years?

reveal.summary: Jon Stewart. Old School hands you Craig Kilborn — the original Daily Show host, whose desk Stewart inherited in January 1999. MTV is where Stewart's television life began, with the network's first talk show. That same year he played Sonny's roommate in Big Daddy. The Daily Show is the institution; the Crossfire quote is the moment he outgrew it; and the tenure — 1999 to 2015 — belongs to exactly one person.
reveal.evidenceToAnswer: The board narrows in stages: Old School plants Kilborn as the obvious theory; MTV clears out the establishment names while sparing the true MTV alumni; the roommate exhibit turns Adam Sandler from answer into signpost; The Daily Show clears half the board but leaves the dangerous desk-mates standing; the Crossfire quote fits only one temperament; and the tenure dates close the case arithmetically.

MTV → The Jon Stewart Show (1993), the network's first talk show

reveal.ohMoment: Craig Kilborn wasn't the answer — he was the arrow. The moment you read '1999 → 2015' and remember who took his desk, every other exhibit snaps into place.

entryPoints.description: Old School and Big Daddy give film fans two doorways; neither requires late-night knowledge.
The Daily Show exhibit and the tenure dates work for anyone who knows the institution's history.
The Crossfire quote is a famous cultural moment in its own right.

editorial.notes: SUSPECT FUNNEL: Old School plants Kilborn as the intended wrong theory and kills Noah; MTV clears Letterman and Leno while deliberately sparing Stiller (a real MTV alum); the roommate exhibit turns Sandler from suspect into signpost; The Daily Show culls the non-desk names but leaves Kilborn, Colbert and the ghost of Noah; the Crossfire quote isolates a temperament; the tenure dates are the smoking gun, kept last. Exactly one CONCLUSIVE exhibit.
